name: Nebraska

regulator.name: Nebraska Secretary of State, Licensing Division

law.name: Nebraska Uniform Athlete Agents Act (Neb. Rev. Stat. 48-2601 to 48-2619)

covers_nil_agents: Yes. An agency contract includes endorsement contracts (Neb. Rev. Stat. 48-2602). The NIL law also names registered athlete agents as allowed representation (48-3602).
summary: Register with the Secretary of State. $300, good for 2 years.

steps.text: Fill out the Athlete Agent Initial Application
steps.detail: Get the affidavit on the last page notarized.
The law lets the Secretary of State set the fee. The current fee is $300.

steps.text: Mail it to the Secretary of State
steps.detail: Attn: Licensing Division, 1201 N St., Ste. 120, Lincoln, NE 68508.

steps.text: Register with each school's compliance office, if it asks
steps.detail: Most schools have their own agent sign-up.

steps.text: Use a written contract with all required items
steps.detail: Your pay and how it's figured, anyone else being paid, expenses, services, length and date signed.

steps.text: Put the warning to the student-athlete in bold capital letters near their signature
steps.detail: Use the exact words the law gives. Nebraska's wording is shorter than most states'.

steps.text: Tell the athlete before they sign that a pro contract may cost them eligibility
steps.detail: Do this out loud or in writing before signing. Skipping it on purpose is a Class I misdemeanor.

steps.text: Give the athlete a copy when they sign
Tell the athletic director in writing within 72 hours of signing
steps.detail: Or before the athlete's next game, whichever comes first. The athlete may cancel within 14 days.

steps.text: Remind the athlete to report each paid NIL deal to their school
steps.detail: This is the athlete's job, not yours. Each school names the person who gets the report.

steps.text: Date the contract the day it's signed
steps.detail: State law and federal law (SPARTA) both ban pre-dating or post-dating it.
Names and addresses of your athletes, every contract and what you spent to recruit each one. The Secretary of State can inspect them.

steps.text: Never give an athlete anything of value before they sign, or make false promises
steps.detail: Also never give anything to anyone else to get an athlete to sign. Nebraska has no 72-hour exception for gifts.
Your registration lasts 2 years. The state sends renewal papers before it runs out.

watch_list.item: Federal Protect College Sports Act of 2026 (S.4668)
watch_list.status: Passed the Senate on Sept 28, 2026. The House is out until Nov 9 and leaders say it won't pass as-is. It dies if not enacted by Jan 3, 2027.
watch_list.impact: It would require every NIL agent to register in a state, cap agent fees at 5% of an endorsement deal and limit contracts to the athlete's eligibility.

watch_list.status: Indefinitely postponed on April 17, 2026. It is dead for this session.
watch_list.impact: It would have added NIL agent rules, like a written fee schedule and a 15-day cancel right.

review_notes: The $300 and $150 fees come from the Secretary of State's instructions, not the statute (the statute lets the state set fees by rule). Confirm in the Rules and Regulations PDF on sos.nebraska.gov/licensing/athlete-agents.
contract_warning: Warning to student-athlete. (1) If you enter into negotiations for, or sign, a professional-sports-services contract, you may lose your eligibility to compete as a student-athlete in your sport; (2) if you have an athletic director, within 72 hours after entering into this contract, both you and your athlete agent must notify your athletic director; and (3) you may cancel this contract within 14 days after signing it.
